marks.gloss_en: Midbar Paran, for Israel were fruitful (paru) and multiplied on it
one who carries out wood [is liable for] enough to cook an easy egg
שנאמר: אם יהיו חטאיכם כשנים כשלג ילבינו
כשנים? כשני מיבעי ליה! -- 'scarlet' should be singular, kashani
kashanim is 'as these years (shanim)' that run from creation until now (= p_kashanim_hashanim)
לכו נא? בואו נא מיבעי ליה! -- God inviting Israel to reason with Him should say 'come', not 'go'
לכו נא אצל אבותיכם ויוכיחו אתכם -- 'go' to your fathers (= p_lechu_etzel_avoteichem)
יאמר ה'? אמר ה' מיבעי ליה! -- the verse should say 'the Lord said', not 'will say'
the mishna: from where [do we know] that one ties a strip of scarlet [on the head of the sent-away goat]? as it says 'if your sins be like scarlet (kashanim), they will be white as snow'
אצל מי נלך? עכשיו יאמר ה' -- 'will say' is Israel's own plea that the Lord now speak (= p_achshav_yomar)

Israel: Master of the world, to whom shall we go? to Abraham, to whom You said 'know for certain' (Gen 15:13), and he did not ask mercy for us? to Isaac, who blessed Esau 'and it shall be when you break loose' (Gen 27:40), and he did not ask mercy for us? to Jacob, to whom You said 'I will go down with you to Egypt' (Gen 46:4), and he did not ask mercy for us?
דכתיב: בחבלי אדם אמשכם בעבתות אהבה -- drawn with cords of love, not iron chains
R' Yochanan: Jacob our father deserved to go down to Egypt in iron chains, but his merit caused [it to be otherwise]
in the future the Holy One will say to Abraham (and then to Jacob, and to Isaac): your children have sinned against Me

Isaac: moreover, how much have they sinned? a man's years are seventy; take away twenty for which You do not punish -- fifty remain; take away twenty-five of nights -- twenty-five remain; take away twelve and a half of praying, eating and the privy -- twelve and a half remain
[we learned:] a reed -- enough to make a quill; if it was thick or crushed -- enough to cook the easiest of eggs, beaten and placed in a pot

ורמינהו: spices ... join with one another; and Chizkiya said: they taught it of sweet kinds, since they are fit to sweeten a pot -- the reason is that they are fit to sweeten; otherwise, not! [so how does the mishna say spices join?]
spices -- two or three names of one kind, or of three kinds and one name -- are forbidden, and they join with one another
